Home / Volunteer at an animal shelter near you

Volunteer at an animal shelter near you

Volunteering is the most reliable way to spend regular time with shelter animals. Most shelters ask volunteers to fill out an application, attend an orientation and commit to a few shifts a month; many then let trained volunteers walk dogs, take them on day trips or hikes, host sleepovers or socialize cats. The programs below include outings open to volunteers or to the public.

Good to know

How do I start volunteering at an animal shelter?

Find a shelter near you below, open its website and look for a Volunteer page. Most have an online application, a minimum age (often 16 or 18) and an orientation session.

Can volunteers walk dogs or take them out?

Usually yes after training. Many shelters' day-out and hiking programs started as volunteer-only programs and some still are; each listing says who can go.

Is there a volunteer dog walking program near me?

Most city, county and nonprofit shelters run one. Search by city on our home page, or ask the shelter about dog walking shifts.

ShelterDayOut is a free directory. We don't run outings or handle bookings; each shelter sets its own rules. Listings are checked monthly, but details change, so confirm with the shelter before you go.

Ready to adopt? ShelterAdoption, our sister site, lists every shelter near you plus upcoming adoption events.
